# shadow/no-lowercase-dom-attrs-casing

Keep DOM attribute spelling consistent: do not mix `class` / `className` (or `for` / `htmlFor`).

`recommended` `fixable`

## Why

ShadowJS accepts both the HTML spelling (`class`, `for`) and the React-style aliases (`className`, `htmlFor`). Using both in one codebase makes search and review harder, and both on one element is ambiguous: the later spread or attribute wins. Pick one (the HTML spelling by default). Misspelled variants such as `classname` or `Class` are not attributes the runtime knows.

## Incorrect

```tsx
<div class='a' className='b' />
```

```tsx
const a = <div class='a' />;
const b = <div className='b' />;
```

```tsx
<div classname='a' />
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor='x' for='y' />
```

## Correct

```tsx
<div class='a' />
```

```tsx
<div className={cls()} />
```

```tsx
<label for='x'>Name</label>
```

## Options

```json
[
  {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "prefer": {
        "enum": [
          "html",
          "react"
        ]
      },
      "enforce": {
        "type": "boolean"
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
]
```

Defaults: `[{"prefer":"html","enforce":false}]`

## Autofix

The fix renames the reported attribute to the preferred spelling (`className` to `class` and `htmlFor` to `for`, or the reverse with `prefer: 'react'`), and a wrong casing to the preferred spelling of its pair (or to `classList`). The same attribute written with two casings is reported without a fix, since the rule cannot tell which one is meant. A wrong casing is fixed only when the element has no other spelling of its attribute, since the rename would write the attribute twice.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/no-lowercase-dom-attrs-casing`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/no-lowercase-dom-attrs-casing */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/no-lowercase-dom-attrs-casing */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. Disable it for a file that mirrors markup from elsewhere (pasted HTML next to ported React) while it is being converted.

## Notes

- Default: only reports mixing (on one element, or both spellings used in one file). The non-preferred spelling is reported.
- Option `prefer` (`html` default, or `react`) chooses the spelling to keep; `enforce: true` reports every non-preferred spelling, even when the file is consistent.
- Also reported: the same attribute written with two casings on one element (`tabIndex` and `tabindex`), and wrong casings of `class`, `className`, `classList`, `for` and `htmlFor`.

## Messages

- `mixedOnElement`: <{{tag}}> has both `{{first}}` and `{{second}}`. Keep one: `{{preferred}}`.
- `mixedInFile`: This file uses both `{{html}}` and `{{react}}`. Use `{{preferred}}` consistently.
- `notPreferred`: Use `{{preferred}}` instead of `{{name}}`.
- `wrongCase`: `{{name}}` is not an attribute the runtime knows. Use `{{preferred}}`.
- `duplicateCasing`: <{{tag}}> sets `{{name}}` and `{{other}}`, which are the same attribute.
